sources.headline: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
sources.text: Kuwait and Bahrain have said they repelled Iranian air attacks overnight as hostilities between Iran and the United States rise.The drone attack on Kuwait was the first in more than two months. The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase, which hosts US forces, but Kuwaiti authorities did not report any damage.It came after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials.Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' state oil firm said a crew member was missing after one of its tankers was attacked in the Gulf waterway on Tuesday.The recent exchanges of fire, as well as deadlock in negotiations on a peace deal, have raised fears of a major escalation in the nine-month-old war.The conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.Since then, Iran has retaliated for US and Israeli strikes by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.It has also attacked dozens of commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass.On Tuesday night, Kuwait's military said its air defences engaged "drone threats" but did not report any casualties or damage.The Kuwaiti foreign ministry condemned the attack, saying it "flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, directly threatened its security and stability, and constituted a grave breach of international law"."The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying," Hani Mohammed, an Egyptian resident of Kuwait, told AFP news agency.Bahrain's military also said on Wednesday that its air defence systems had "intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks".The island kingdom, which hosts the US Navy's 5th Fleet, has reported four attacks over the past six days, following a two-month lull.Qatar, which has mediated in the stalled indirect talks between Iran and the US, said the Iranian attacks on its neighbours were a "dangerous escalation that threatens to complicate efforts aimed at containing tensions".The Iranian army said its drones had targeted US Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait.Later, the army's commander-in-chief, Maj Gen Amir Hatami, warned the US and its allies that it would respond more forcefully to any new attacks on Iran."If the enemy repeats its mistake... we have the readiness and the plans to confront it and its supporters in a stronger, more crushing way and without geographic limitations," he said.On Tuesday night, US fighter jets targeted a missile launch site on Qeshm Island "with precision munitions" in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets", US military officials said.Iranian media reported explosions on the island but cited a local official as saying they had caused no damage to infrastructure.In a separate development, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (Adnoc) said a search-and-rescue operation was under way for a missing sailor following an attack on one of its vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The rest of the crew were safely evacuated and 11 were receiving medical care, it added.The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre reported that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles (24km) north of Khasab, in Oman's Musandam peninsula. It said the attack caused a fire on board that was extinguished.Iran said two oil tankers and a ship carrying liquefied natural gas (LNG) had caught fire after hitting naval mines while sailing along an "authorised route".At least 25 seafarers have been killed across the Middle East since the start of the war, when the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports.The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the conflict and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.In recent months, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling through the Strait of Hormuz, allowing crude oil exports from Gulf states to reach around 80% of pre-war levels, according to analysts.

sources.headline: Kuwait, Bahrain face new Iran attacks after US strike on Qeshm Island
sources.text: Iranian attacks on the Gulf countries draw condemnation from across the region.Iran has launched new attacks on its Gulf neighbours, targeting an airbase used by the United States military in Kuwait and carrying out several attacks on Bahrain after the US bombed Iran’s Qeshm Island.Kuwait said it activated its air defences to counter drone strikes – the first since early September – and Bahrain said it fended off an Iranian attack early on Wednesday, a day after the US attacked a missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Kuwait reports drone attacks as Iran, US trade attacks on Qeshm and Bahrainlist 2 of 3Piecemeal wars: A new kind of world war is already under waylist 3 of 3Can the US and Iran sustain a ‘frozen war’?end of listThe US said it carried out the strike in response to an Iranian attack on a US radar installation in Bahrain earlier on Tuesday.Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy’s 5th Fleet, has experienced four Iranian attacks in six days, ending a weeks-long respite in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.Iran said its recent attacks were in response to US drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers.The uptick in fighting raises the risk of a wider escalation towards the resumption of all-out conflict nearly nine months into the war, and complicates negotiations for a diplomatic solution, which have stagnated despite intensified mediation efforts from Qatar.A municipal employee stands next to military drones on display at Baharestan Square in Tehran on September 28, 2026 [Atta Kenare/AFP]Gulf and Arab condemnationThe Iranian attacks on the Gulf countries have drawn condemnation from across the region.Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain “in the strongest terms” and denounced an attack on a tanker belonging to the United Arab Emirates.The ministry said the kingdom rejects Iran’s disruption of shipping routes and urged a negotiated solution.Arab League chief Nabil Fahmy said the repeated attacks on Arab countries reveal “a continuous escalation pattern that threatens to widen the circle of confrontation”. He also condemned the targeting of a ship belonging to the UAE’s national oil company, ADNOC, as it crossed the Strait of Hormuz.Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, the Gulf Cooperation Council’s secretary-general, held Iran “responsible for this escalation and its repercussions on regional security”.Qatar’s Foreign Ministry called the attacks “a dangerous escalation” that risks undermining diplomatic efforts. Kuwait and the UAE also condemned them.Kuwait’s Foreign Ministry described the drone attacks as flagrant violations of its sovereignty and a direct threat to its security, Al Jazeera’s Zein Basravi reported from Doha.Basravi also said Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesman, Majed al-Ansari, warned that continued escalation without restraint from both the US and Iran makes a negotiated solution, or even continued dialogue, harder.Meanwhile, Iran’s army chief, Major-General Amir Hatami, said the armed forces were “monitoring the enemy’s movements” after a third US aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East, the Fars news agency reported.He said Iran’s response to any misstep by the US and its “backers” would be “even more crushing”.

sources.headline: US strikes Iranian island after Tehran targets Bahrain
sources.text: The US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said it targeted a US military radar system in Bahrain, despite talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.

sources.headline: U.S. launches strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in Strait of Hormuz
sources.text:
6:59 PM / November 17, 2026
Kuwait military says it's facing "hostile drone attacks"
Kuwait's military on Tuesday said it was hitting back at "hostile drone attacks," urging the public to follow security and safety advice."The General Staff of the Army notes that any explosion sounds heard are the result of air defense systems intercepting hostile attacks," the Kuwaiti army wrote on X. No other details were provided, and no one has claimed responsibility for the attack.Kuwait is among U.S. allies in the Middle East that have faced attacks from Iran since the start of the war. Earlier Tuesday, Bahrain said its air defense systems had successfully intercepted Iranian drones as Iran claimed to have struck a U.S. radar system in the kingdom.CBS/AFP
5:23 PM / November 17, 2026
Man convicted in Iran-backed plot to murder Trump gets 27.5 years in prison
A Pakistani man who was convicted of attempted terrorism and orchestrating a murder-for-hire plot at the direction of Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps, with potential targets including President Trump and former President Joe Biden, was sentenced to 27 1/2 years in federal prison on Tuesday.Asif Merchant was convicted in March — shortly after the start of the Iran war — on terrorism and murder-for-hire charges and faced up to life in prison. Merchant shuffled into court with a serious expression and shackled ankles, peering around the room. He had wavy gray hair and wore a tan prison outfit. He pressed a headphone to his ear, for an Urdu translation of the proceedings, watching the judge intently and bobbing in his chair as he learned his fate.Read more here.
2:38 PM / November 17, 2026
U.S. announces "self-defense" strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
The U.S. launched precision strikes on an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a U.S. military official.The official said the strike was launched "in self-defense." "The strike was in response to IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets," the official said. "U.S. Central Command remains highly vigilant and fully postured to protect Americans across the region."While the official did not specifically mention the IRGC aggression, the strikes came hours after Iran targeted a U.S. radar site in Bahrain. The strikes were successfully intercepted, according to U.S. Central Command. This was the third attempted strike by Iran on a U.S. military installation in the last five days. All of them were intercepted, U.S. officials said.Iran had earlier said the U.S. attacked Qeshm Island, but they "caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas," according to Ahmad Nafisi, deputy provincial governor of the southern province of Hormozgan, quoted by the official IRNA news agency.
An infographic showing Qeshm Island created on Nov. 3, 2026.
Omar Zaghloul/Anadolu via Getty Images
2:17 PM / November 17, 2026
Iraq resumes pumping oil through pipeline to Turkey in order to avoid Strait of Hormuz
Iraq has resumed pumping oil to Turkey through a pipeline at an initial capacity of 120,000 barrels a day, Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair al-Abadi said Tuesday in comments carried by state media. The export capacity will be gradually increased to reach 500,000 barrels a day, he said.The capacity is fairly small compared to other pipelines in the region. The Saudi East-West pipeline, which crosses from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea in order to avoid the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Strait, has a capacity of 7 million barrels per day.In August, Iraq and Turkey signed a deal to increase oil exports through a pipeline to the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.Iraq is moving to strengthen the resilience of its oil export infrastructure following the U.S.-Iran war's disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.The Iraq-Turkey pipeline has been largely idle since 2023 following legal and commercial disputes.AP/CBS
1:52 PM / November 17, 2026
Qatar says U.S.-Iran mediation efforts continue
Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari said Tuesday that mediation efforts between the U.S. and Iran were continuing and a meeting with the Iranian side would be held later in the day to exchange views on proposals under discussion.He warned any escalation on the ground posed an "extremely grave danger" to the prospects of reaching an agreement.Earlier, President Trump said Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before" if it follows through on its reported desire to set off a dirty bomb in Washington, D.C. — a claim denied by Iranian officials.Mr. Trump made the remark after being quizzed by reporters about whether there was an imminent threat to Washington from Iran."I hope it's not. But we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy," said Mr. Trump, who was meeting with leaders of Japan, India and Australia in the Philippines.AP/CBS
1:20 PM / November 17, 2026
Houthis say they targeted crucial Saudi East-West oil pipeline in drone attacks
The Iran-backed Houthi militant group in Yemen said it carried out successful drone strikes Tuesday on the Saudi East-West pipeline.Pumping Station No. 9, west of Riyadh, was allegedly targeted in two phases with three one-way attack drones, the Houthis said. They then targeted Pumping Station No. 8 with two drones. The Houthis claimed they made "precise and direct" hits on the pumping stations.The Saudis had earlier said they shot down a Houthi drone near Riyadh but it was unclear if it was related to the attack on the East-West pipeline.The pipeline, which is comprised of 11 pumping stations, was previously targeted in a drone attack on Sept. 11, which knocked out the line for nearly two weeks. That attack was blamed on Iran-backed rebel groups located in northern Iraq.The pipeline gives the Saudis a way to avoid the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Strait and instead take oil north in the Red Sea out of the Suez Canal. The 750-mile pipeline, built in the 1980s, consists of two separate pipes carrying a maximum capacity of 7 million barrels of oil per day.
Infographic with map showing route of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which can transport up to 7 million barrels of oil per day and bypass the chokepoints of Bab-al-Mandab and the Strait of Hormuz.
Patricio Arana/AFP via Getty Images
12:46 PM / November 17, 2026
Saudis shoot down Houthi drone near Riyadh, coalition says
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthi militia intercepted and shot down a drone near Riyadh on Tuesday, the spokesperson for the group, Col. Turki Al-Malki, said on X.The Houthis have regularly fired one-way attack drones at Riyadh since the civil war in Yemen restarted this summer. The Houthis have been fighting Saudi-backed Yemeni forces aligned with the internationally recognized government.This was the fourth straight day the Houthis had fired attack drones into Saudi Arabia, but all of them were intercepted, according to the coalition. The Saudi coalition said it intercepted two drones in the Mecca and Riyadh regions on Monday as well as four separate Houthi drone attacks across the country on Sunday.
12:10 PM / November 17, 2026
U.S.-Israeli war has created "horrific" situation for Iranians, Amnesty International says
Iranian authorities have intensified their repression of the country's population in response to the Middle East war, which began weeks after their deadly crackdown on anti-government protests killed thousands of people, Amnesty International said on Tuesday.An internet blackout imposed at the time of the crackdown on Jan. 8 and 9 and the scale of the casualties meant it was not yet possible for the group to quantify the number of people killed, Amnesty's lead Iran researcher, Raha Bahreini, said.But she told AFP in an interview that "there is no doubt that thousands were massacred in less than 48 hours."She added that the Middle East war, which began with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb. 28, "with Iranians still reeling from the January massacres, created a horrific situation for the people in the country.""The authorities used the cover of wartime conditions to intensify repression," she said.Bahreini lamented the international community had shifted its attention away from the Iranian people to the geopolitical consequences of the conflict."The massacres that took place in January, which should have moved then global consciousness, have faded away from attention," she said.
11:46 AM / November 17, 2026
Iran's foreign minister refers to dirty bomb report as "RUBBISH"
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi slammed reports that his country was targeting Washington, D.C., with chemical weapons or building missiles under dams, blaming the reports on Israel. "In the past 72 hours, pro-Israel media have 'reported' that Iran is supposedly plotting to use chemical weapons in DC while building missile bases under dams. sources.headline: US strikes Iran’s Qeshm island in Strait of Hormuz after Guards target Bahrain
sources.text: TEHRAN - The United States struck Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 17, hours after Tehran’s Revolutionary Guards said they launched an attack on a base in Bahrain used by Washington.The strait – a key route for oil and gas shipments – has become the focus of the stalemated Middle East war, with the US military working to protect ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Iran’s attempts to close it.Outright fighting in the war, which began in late February, has largely subsided, but there has been no peace deal and the United States continues to blockade Iranian ports, cutting off its oil exports and hammering its economy.US fighter jets “used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island”, an American official told AFP on condition of anonymity, adding that the strike was in response to Iranian “aggression targeting US personnel and assets.”Iran’s official IRNA news agency had earlier cited a regional official as saying the United States had hit the island without causing serious damage.Despite Washington and Tehran holding back from a full resumption of hostilities, tensions remain high.On Nov 17, US President Donald Trump said he was taking “very seriously” reports that Iran was developing plans to use a so-called “dirty bomb” in Washington.CNN cited seven anonymous US officials as saying Iran was plotting how to target senior administration figures with a bomb laced with chemical or radioactive material, though they stopped short of saying Iran planned to carry out such an attack.“If there is (such a threat), they will pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before,” Trump said, adding: “I hope it’s not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy.”Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed the report and called it “Iraq War-style propaganda”.‘Exercise restraint’Earlier on Nov 17, explosions boomed across Bahrain’s capital as a mobile phone alert warned residents to seek safety.Bahrain’s armed forces said they “confronted, intercepted and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today... before they could achieve their objectives”, while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US-operated radar system.“Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain,” the Guards’ Sepah news website said.The attack was in response to the “repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones”, it added. The Guards also said they had intercepted and captured a US drone south of Qeshm.Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, was heavily targeted earlier in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, but had not been hit for weeks until Iranian drone attacks on Nov 13 and 15.“I was on my way to work when the warning sirens went on,” Abdulrahman Abdullah, a Bahraini civil servant in his forties, told AFP on Nov 17.“Fear and anxiety rise as attacks increase... We hope things will go back to how they were.”‘Pushing the envelope’The violence came as the United States moved the USS Theodore Roosevelt into the region, bringing the number of American carrier strike groups in the region to three.The deployment adds to an already large US naval presence, which includes two other supercarriers – the George H W Bush and the George Washington – and more than a dozen destroyers.Iranian drone attacks have resumed ahead of this week’s unprecedented trilateral summit between Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts.Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will discuss “world peace” at the talks in Shenzhen, according to China. Trump has said he plans to discuss the Iran war at the meeting.Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy MENA analytica called the flare-up in Middle East violence a “deliberate testing of boundaries rather than an immediate return to full-scale warfare”.“Both Washington and Tehran are pushing the envelope, probing each other’s red lines and trying to establish how far they can escalate without provoking a response that spirals beyond their control,” he said. AFP
